records.subject: Concern over delay in Recruitment Process for Gojri and Pahari Teaching Posts in the universities of the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Gulam Ali: I draw attention of the Government to the continued delay in completing the recruitment process for Assistant Professor posts in Gojri and Pahari subjects in the universities of the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir.? Gojri and Pahari are languages belonging to the people mentioned under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, and their promotion and academic development are constitutional obligations. Neglecting recruitment in these subjects weakens academic standards and marginalises large linguistic communities. These teaching posts have been notified along with other subjects no. of times since 2013. While the recruitment process for other subjects has been completed, interviews for Gojri and Pahari alone have not been held. This has adversely affected students, research scholars, and qualified candidates associated with these subjects. It must also be acknowledged that speakers of Gojri and Pahari have made significant sacrifices in the fight against militancy and have consistently contributed to national security, peace, and stability in the region. Ignoring their languages in academic institutions sends a discouraging message to communities that have stood firmly with the nation. I therefore urge the Government to ensure that pending interviews are conducted at the earliest, so that justice is done and both Gojri and Pahari languages get their due.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over non-implementation of livestock promotion schemes for the Pastoral community of J&K.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Gulam Ali:

?The Gujjar?Bakarwal community is a traditional pastoral group whose primary livelihood depends on rearing sheep and goats. Livestock forms the backbone of their economy and sustenance. Therefore, government schemes promoting livestock development are critically important for their welfare. The Government has introduced programmes such as the National Livestock Mission and the Holistic Rural Development Programme to enhance productivity, commercialization, and income of livestock-dependent communities. However, despite their relevance, the Gujjar?Bakarwal community has largely been unable to access these benefits, particularly in the Jammu division. District targets were fixed for establishing livestock units, yet applications from this community are often ignored or delayed. Under the Public Good category of 525 units, not a single unit has been allotted to members of this community. Although procedures are simple, applications are not processed efficiently, leading to exclusion from schemes meant for their upliftment. A district-wise review of beneficiaries should be conducted. Special facilitation camps must be organized in pastoral areas. Time-bound processing mechanisms and accountability measures should be enforced. Priority consideration for pastoral communities may also be introduced. Ensuring equitable access is essential for socio-economic upliftment and sustainable livestock development in the region. This will help bridge gaps in implementation, ensure fair representation, strengthen livelihoods, reduce marginalization, improve trust in institutions, and enable the community to fully participate in development initiatives and national growth processes effectively and sustainably going forward ahead. I urge Government to look into it.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand to combat drug menace through community participation.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Gulam Ali: I rise to draw the attention of Government to the alarming drug menace plaguing Jammu and Kashmir. An estimated 1.35 million people in J&K (about 8% of the population) are affected by substance abuse. Sir, 90% of these drug users are youth between 17 and 33 years old. The proliferation of opioids (especially heroin) has created a public health crisis; for instance, shared needles have driven Hepatitis C prevalence to nearly 20% among injecting drug users. Law enforcement alone cannot curb this epidemic, which is eating away at our social fabric. The need of the hour is a massive community-driven fightback against drugs. We cannot succeed unless the fight becomes a public movement involving all sections of society. I urge the Government to facilitate the formation of village-level anti-drug committees. Empowering local leaders, teachers, religious heads, and especially women, in dedicated anti-drug committees will help combat the menace at the grassroots. Notably, women can play a pivotal role in rehabilitation and awareness; setting up all-women anti-drug committees and support groups will help destigmatize addiction and save our youth.??????????? Furthermore, there is a need to strengthen rehabilitation infrastructure. There is no proper arrangement or policy for rehabilitating drug addicts in J&K, leading many to relapse after detoxification. Therefore, I urge the Government to establish a comprehensive rehabilitation policy increase the number of de-addiction centres, ensure follow-up tracking of recovered individuals, and reintegrate them via skill training.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for republication of Indian Arabic Magazine “Thaqafatul Hind” by Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).
records.SM_Text:
Shri Gulam Ali: The Indian Arabic magazine ?Thaqafatul Hind?, launched in 1950 by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), played a pivotal role in promoting Indian civilization, culture, history, religion, art, festivals and literature in the Arab world. It featured Arabic translations of Indian short stories, poetry, and scholarly articles, becoming a key reference for researchers and academics in Arab countries. Distributed through Indian embassies to universities and libraries across the region, the magazine served as a bridge between India and the Arab world, countering misconceptions and strengthening India?s cultural identity. Published regularly from 1950 to 2017, ?Thaqafatul Hind? ceased to be published in 2017, leaving a significant void in India?s cultural diplomacy. Today, as India strengthens its ties with Arab nations, particularly the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, the revival of this magazine is essential. It would not only highlight India?s rich cultural heritage and historical depth but also foster stronger people-to-people connections. Importantly, the magazine was never limited to any specific community. It represented India?s shared heritage and diversity. Given its historical significance and the growing importance of cultural diplomacy, I urge the Government of India and the ICCR to take steps to revive ?Thaqafatul Hind?. Its republication will reinforce India?s intellectual and cultural presence in the Arab world, contributing to deeper mutual understanding and stronger bilateral relations.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for inclusion of Gojri language in the 8th schedule of the constitution
records.SM_Text:
Shri Gulam Ali: As per article 344 and 351, the 8th schedule was intended to promote the progressive use of Hindi and for the enrichment and promotion of other languages. Initially 14 languages were added and later on in 1967, 1992 and 2004, few other comparatively lesser spoken languages were added and as on today, there are 22 languages in the 8th? schedule of the Constitution of India. The inclusion of the languages in the 8th? schedule has not been on the basis of them being widely spoken. Even sindhi, which is spoken by only 0.003% of people is included in 8th? schedule and so is Manipuri, bodo and Nepali. However, the Gojri language which is spoken by more than 3% of Indians is not included in 8th? schedule even though spoken across all the northern states of India. This has resulted in deep-seated resentment and discontentment among the Gujjars residing in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, UP, MP, HP and JK. Although, through various committees, criteria was tried to be fixed for inclusion of the languages in the 8th? schedule, but no uniform criteria could be agreed upon. The only one criteria which should prevail in inclusion of a language in 8th? schedule should be its widespread use like the Gojri which is spoken in almost half of India in the northern states and even Arab, Europe, Afghanistan and Pakistan and as such I demand that Gojri should be included in the 8th schedule of the Constitution of India.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for Establishment of Fodder Corporation of India to Fight Stubble Burning.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI GULAM ALI (Nominated):? Establishment of a Fodder Corporation of India, modelled after the successful Food Corporation of India, is imperative to combat the escalating menace of environmental degradation, the adverse effects of stubble burning and scarcity of fodder.? The agricultural and animal husbandry sectors, crucial components of India?s economy, face a pressing challenge with the traditional practice of burning stubble/crop residues, scarcity of fodder, high prices and animal dying due to hunger, contributing significantly to air pollution and animal devoid of adequate fodder.? A dedicated Fodder Corporation would play a pivotal role in addressing this issue by promoting sustainable agricultural practices. It could incentivize farmers to adopt alternative methods for managing crop residues, such as converting them into fodder for livestock. By establishing efficient collection centres and processing units, the Corporation can streamline the conversion of crop residues into nutrient-rich fodder, reducing the reliance on environmentally harmful practices like stubble burning.

????????? Moreover, the Fodder Corporation can act as a catalyst for rural development by creating employment opportunities and promoting the use of eco-friendly technologies. By integrating modern farming techniques and providing training to farmers, the Corporation can enhance agricultural productivity while mitigating the environmental impact of traditional practices.? In essence, the establishment of a Fodder corporation of India is not just a necessity but a strategic imperative for fostering sustainable agriculture, preserving the environment, and safeguarding the well-being of future generations. It represents a forward-thinking approach to balance agricultural needs with environmental conservation, ensuring a harmonious coexistence between farming practices and ecological integrity.?

????????? I urge the Government to establish Fodder Corporation of India.

(Ends)

records.subject: Regarding non-deposit of tax deducted from the income of the assessee by their employer.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI GULAM ALI: Madam, this is to bring to your kind consideration that certain taxpayers are facing some income tax related hardships on account of non‑deposit of tax deducted at source to Government account by tax deductors which does not come to the notice of Central Processing Centre (CPC) of the Income Tax Department and when the assessee approaches the Jurisdictional Income Tax Officer with such problems, the Jurisdictional Officer expresses his inability to take any action against the defaulters claiming that the Income Tax Officer cannot do unless the same comes from CPC.? In one such instance, the TDS of a taxpayer was deducted by a Government Corporation/JMC but was not deposited during the relevant year in Jammu and Kashmir. The assessee had offered his correct Income for tax to the Income Tax Department and calculated proper taxes. Credit of TDS was not received on account of non‑deposit of the tax deducted by the deductor. As a result, the Department served the person demand notice of the amount of tax which was deducted out of the income of the person but was not deposited by the said Government Corporation during the relevant year. Same may have been done with the other assessees by various departments/corporations across India.? I, therefore, urge the Government to seek data on such complaints and redress them.

(Ends)

records.subject: Demand for fixing a timeline and ensuring timely completion of Transmission and Distribution Projects in the Power Sector in the UT of Jammu & Kashmir.
records.SM_Text:
SHRI GULAM ALI (Nominated): Sir, I would like to thank the Government of India and Shri R.K. Singh, Minister for Power, for his personal intervention in the improvement of power sector in Jammu & Kashmir. It is because of the Prime Ministers special focus that hydroelectric projects like Kiru-Kawar, Pakkal-Dul and Rattle on the Chenab Basin, with a combined capacity of around 3,000 megawatt, are in the process of execution. This capacity is equivalent to the capacity addition in Jammu & Kashmir over the last 75 years. The Government of India has also been generous towards implementation of transmission and distribution projects in the Union Territory under various centrally sponsored schemes the fruits of which are already beginning to be felt. To anchor the gains achieved in this sector, the Government of India has already granted technical sanction for a transmission plan for Jammu & Kashmir costing around Rs. 4,971 crore, vide letter no. CEA-PS-11-22(15)/1/2018-PSPA-1 Division-Part(1), dated 18.06.2021. Implementation of this plan within the next two to three years is very essential to ensure that quality power is available 24X7 to the people of Jammu & Kashmir. I would request the hon. Minister to fix a time-line for the Government for implementation of the projects in the transmission sector in Jammu & Kashmir and strategy of their funding. As I have already mentioned that these projects should come up in next 2-3 years for enabling the fruits of the hitherto investment in power sector of Jammu and Kashmir to reach the consumers. I, therefore, urge upon the Government to fix a timeline for implementation of transmission and distribution projects in the U.T. of Jammu and Kashmir and ensure its timely completion. Thank you, Sir.

(Ends)
